purpose: Evaluate calibrated evidence for one declared fault hypothesis against a no-fault null as samples arrive, while preserving Type-I error control under optional stopping.

model.likelihood_table: A fixed categorical outcome distribution under a simple null and one simple alternative, for one frozen evidence channel.
model.statistic: log E_t = sum_{i=1}^t log(P_alternative(X_i) / P_null(X_i)); E_t = exp(log E_t).
model.decision: Cross the per-alternative threshold when E_t >= 1 / alpha_i; return model_conditional_evidence_threshold_crossed, never a physical-cause or operating-safety claim.
model.null_support: Every listed outcome has positive null probability. An observed outcome outside the frozen support poisons the session; zero-null-probability observations are never turned into infinite evidence.
model.replay: Each receipt binds outcome, timestamp, sample index, model, calibration, input receipt, prior receipt, log e-value and threshold.

familywise_control.allocation: alpha_i = floor(familywise_alpha_ppm / alternative_count); sum_i alpha_i <= familywise_alpha_ppm.
familywise_control.dependence_between_alternatives: No independence assumption is required for the Bonferroni family-wise bound, but each individual null e-process must remain valid.

comparators.method: Evaluate a predeclared fixed-size sample window, then decide once.
Accumulate the same simple-null/simple-alternative likelihood ratio with a fixed decision schedule.
The proposed process can be inspected after every accepted sample and stopped at any data-dependent time; threshold is governed by Ville's inequality under the validity conditions.
Measure average expected posterior entropy reduction; this is an evidence-acquisition utility, not a Type-I error guarantee.
Compare asymptotic pairwise mode separation under repeated observations; this is not a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee.

validity_conditions.observations: Current v0.1 requires repeated conditionally independent outcome draws from the declared fixed likelihood law under the null; nonstationary or serially dependent data need conditional likelihood models or a separately validated e-process.
validity_conditions.channel: One frozen channel, sensor semantics, operating regime and likelihood table per session. Changing channel selection within a session is not supported.
validity_conditions.model: The null and alternative likelihood distributions are fixed before confirmatory observations; both are normalized and every supported outcome has positive probability under each.
validity_conditions.calibration: Likelihoods require independent calibration and review. Hashes bind inputs but do not authenticate reviewer identity or prove calibration.
validity_conditions.optional_stopping: Under a valid nonnegative null e-process, Ville's inequality gives P(sup_t E_t >= 1/alpha_i) <= alpha_i, so users may inspect or stop at any sample without inflating the individual test's Type-I error.
validity_conditions.multiple_faults: Bonferroni allocation across the declared alternative count bounds the probability of any false fault alarm under the shared no-fault null by the family-wise alpha budget.

hard_gates: the null and alternative IDs, channel, model digest, calibration digest and outcome likelihood table are frozen before confirmatory testing
null and alternative outcome probabilities each sum to one and every listed outcome has positive null probability
the sequential likelihood-ratio increment is computed in log space and replayed from every observation receipt
an unsupported observed category poisons the session rather than producing infinite evidence
the sample stream is contiguous and the same evidence channel and likelihood table are used for the entire session
the likelihood model is checked for calibration on independent episodes and remains within its declared operating regime
the null outcome distribution is conditionally correct for the observed history; i.i.d./stationary assumptions are not silently assumed under drift
Bonferroni per-alternative alpha is no greater than the allocated family-wise budget divided by the number of tested alternatives
the optional-stopping claim is conditional on the null e-process validity conditions and does not imply protection against misspecification
a threshold crossing is a statistical flag for the declared model pair, not unique physical cause isolation or a maintenance/operating instruction
a changed channel, controller mode, calibration, likelihood version or unsupported regime requires a new evidence session and model identity
receipt integrity is not signer authentication, trusted time or proof of physical sensor truth

research_targets_not_achieved.target: Across frozen no-fault replay episodes with predeclared optional stopping rules, empirical family-wise false-alarm probability remains at or below the configured bound within independent-episode uncertainty.
Improve median and p95 fault-event detection latency versus the fixed-window baseline at the same family-wise false-alarm budget, on matched independent episodes.
100% receipt-chain and log-evidence replay on all accepted samples, with zero unsupported outcomes treated as infinite evidence.
Zero valid e-process threshold-crossing claims after the frozen model or channel leaves its reviewed support; unsupported regimes remain not_evaluated or start a separately calibrated session.

evidence_boundaries.implementation: src/sequential_evidence.rs is source-authored; no real engine likelihood model is calibrated or evaluated.
evidence_boundaries.validity: The optional-stopping guarantee is mathematical and model-conditional; synthetic unit tests do not validate real-world conditional independence or likelihood calibration.
evidence_boundaries.non_authority: A crossed threshold is not physical proof, unique isolation, maintenance authority, controller write permission or ODD clearance.
evidence_boundaries.cross_engine: A single engine test-bench cannot establish cross-engine or fleet validity.

claim_ceiling: Synthetic likelihood-ratio mechanics and receipt replay only until the likelihood model is calibrated, independent null episodes are audited, event-level comparator runs are completed and temporal-dependence assumptions are reviewed.
